[1/4] Plan: backup.verify hashes every source file against its copy and reports missing/different/extra; python -m photo_harbor backup --to DIR --check exits 1 on problems; Harbor window Check backup runs it in a thread; tests, README, ADR-016

impact_assessment.why: Mirroring only compares sizes; a silent bit-rot or truncation on the backup drive is invisible, and the user has no way to know the second copy is good
impact_assessment.benefits: A real integrity check with a clear report; no server dependency, no schema change, and no writes to either drive
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --check flag and window button; dependency: hashlib only; concurrency: read-only walk while backup may run; state: none persisted
impact_assessment.mitigation: Skip dot folders like mirror does, stream hashes in 1 MB blocks, cap the printed problem list while counting every file, and run the window check on a background thread

[3/4] CLI backup --check prints the report and exits 1 on damage; Harbor window Check backup runs it on a background thread and re-enables itself; manual temp run verified clean 0 and damaged 1

impact_assessment.why: Months are the only date axis; finding a specific trip that crosses a month boundary, or a single day, takes scrolling
impact_assessment.benefits: Exact date windows combine with person, kind, album, favorites and name search; no schema change and no new dependency
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two new query parameters and scope keys; dependency: none; concurrency: read-only filter; state: dates are client-only and reset with other scopes
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate the date shape and order before querying, keep substr comparisons for correctness with existing sort_time, and reset dates whenever another scope is chosen

impact_assessment.why: The gallery is always newest-first; finding the oldest photo or the files taking the most space means a different tool or scrolling
impact_assessment.benefits: One control over the existing page query; no schema change, no extra read, and it combines with every filter
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one new query parameter and scope key; dependency: none; concurrency: read-only; state: sort is client-only and resets on person/month/favorites changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate against a fixed set, keep a stable sha tiebreaker on every order, and preserve the chosen order when a date window is applied

[1/4] Plan: catalog format 6 adds a trash table; TrashBook moves one person's copy into .harbor/trash with a row, forgets the copy, restores through store.ingest, and deletes permanently; API list/move/restore/delete/empty; Trash tab and move actions; tests, dogfood, ADR-019, README

impact_assessment.why: There is no way to remove a bad or unwanted photo from Harbor without using Explorer; direct deletion would be irreversible and would desynchronise the catalog
impact_assessment.benefits: A safe, per-person remove with restore; shared photos stay for others; no permanent loss on the first action; trash is hidden from the library and backup
impact_assessment.risks: contract: catalog format 6 and new endpoints; dependency: none; concurrency: moves and catalog writes share the store lock; state: trash rows and files, with a crash window between move and forget
impact_assessment.mitigation: Insert the trash row before moving, move inside the store lock, roll back the file if forgetting fails, restore by re-ingesting the bytes through the normal hash-verified path, and test shared/last-copy cases plus migration
